scope: Every top-level incoming dispatcher case; method-scoped normal CFG, conservative exception CFG, and intraprocedural receiver provenance. Delegated/deferred consumers require the separately reviewed annex; no complete server schema is inferred.

counts_across_case_paths.unit: Sum of getter instruction observations separately reachable from each opcode entry; shared handlers such as 708/755 count for each opcode.

checks.exception_model: Conservative edges from every instruction in each protected interval; extra reachability is an upper bound, not proof that every handler executes.

reviewed_delegated_alias_and_dynamic_ann.finding: The aj.c(ay) call receives the cached icon packet returned by aj.g(int), not the current 208 response. Its image fields must not be merged into the 208 response schema.
Current packet is queued in aj.bW by aj.a(ay), returned by aj.ai(), and later read by the UI: tag 4 text for display and tag 5 text for the accepted URL.

Response is stored as aj.aD, then tag 30 is read through that alias. All three reads are already in all_getter_reads, but direct_response_read is false because the extractor recognizes only an immediate array-load sequence. The null branch repeats the same getter and unboxes it; no optional-field guarantee follows.

Current response is passed to aj.c(ay), which reads tag 1 as byte and tags 2 through 6 as image byte arrays. Success passes the same response to aj.d(ay), which reads tag 1 before caching serialized bytes.

j.a(ay) serializes the entire incoming resource; its own tag 1 reads target settings j.a, not this packet. Dispatcher installs current response as aj.j. Subsequent consumers use dynamic integer/presence/image accessors; login reads config tag 1 as the revision. An empty dispatcher direct_fields array does not mean an empty config schema.
reviewed_delegated_alias_and_dynamic_ann.limit: This audits packet forwarding and generic accessors. It does not infer every UI theme key or meaning from all call sites.

reviewed_delegated_alias_and_dynamic_ann.finding: Three direct current-response text getters are absent even from all_getter_reads because the tag is computed. The loop starts i=0, iterates i<field_count, and reads only when i%3==1.
reviewed_delegated_alias_and_dynamic_ann.limit: Field count is not maximum tag; dense triples are a client assumption, not a recovered server validation rule.

reviewed_delegated_alias_and_dynamic_ann.finding: aj.b(ay) persists the whole response, installs it as aj.s, and reads tag 1 text into settings. Later y.e(int) reads a dynamic text tag from aj.s. Dispatcher itself also reads tag 1 before sending language confirmation.
reviewed_delegated_alias_and_dynamic_ann.limit: The runtime lookup accepts dynamic resource IDs; dispatcher direct_fields is not a complete language-resource schema.

interpretation_notes: All 55 rows reproduce and match the extractor scope. This is not a finding that their fields are a complete wire schema.
906 alias getters already occur in all_getter_reads. Only direct_fields excludes them. 1002 dynamic getters are absent from all_getter_reads itself.
203 tags 31/32 have multiple value interpretations. Raw binary fields carry no discriminator, so simultaneous typed views do not prove impossible serialization.
203 tags 33/35/37 use a byte presence guard then an integer value read. 421/423 tag 3 uses text presence then a long value read. These differ from multiple semantic value uses.
Field-view presence/value labels classify immediate null checks versus other uses; they do not establish requiredness, complete semantic use, or server validation.
The conservative exception-edge audit adds no dispatcher typed getter sites for any opcode. Error effects remain distinct from field discovery.
The normal CFG follows both sides of branches; it is not a proof that every path is feasible for one concrete packet.
